newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurdish leader and U.S. official to talk.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurdish leader and U.S. official to talk.

text.p: The Iraqi Kurdish faction leader who seized control of northern Iraq with military help from Baghdad this month was expected to meet a senior U.S. official in Ankara for tough talks on Wednesday evening.

Massoud Barzani first met Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller but then gave reporters the slip in a car chase through Ankara on his way to a meeting at an unknown location with U.S. assistant secretary of state Robert Pelletreau.
Washington was expected to try to dissuade Barzani from further cooperation with Iraqi President Saddam Hussein in a bid to pick up the pieces of its shattered policy on north Iraq.

Barzani, leader of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), has said he turned to Saddam for help against his Kurdish rivals, led by Jalal Talabani, because they were backed by Iran and the United States had failed to intervene.

The KDP's London spokesman, Dilshad Miran, said on Tuesday that Barzani planned to tell the United States he was not interested in further deals with Iraq and that he wanted the United States and its allies to continue their air operation, using bases in Turkey, to protect northern Iraq from Saddam.
Barzani ditched the United States and forged an alliance with Saddam last month despite a history of bloody Iraqi attacks on the Kurdish population in the north.
Diplomats said they were sceptical about Barzani's stated intentions.

Pelletreau will "repeat the advice privately that we have tried to give Mr Barzani and Mr Talabani in public...that Mr Barzani's relationship with Saddam Hussein cannot be in the long-term interest of his people or himself," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Tuesday.

Senior KDP official Sami Abderrahman said Barzani had "a very good meeting" with Ciller, but made no comment about the meeting to be held with Pelletreau. Barzani's aides said the KDP leader was heading for talks with Pelletreau.
U.S. officials in Ankara were unavailable for comment.
A Western diplomat said British diplomats would also attend the meeting.
"The Americans will want assurances that Saddam will not take over northern Iraq," the source said.

Barzani's KDP, backed by Iraqi troops and tanks, captured the Kurdish city of Arbil from the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK)last month, shattering a U.S.-brokered ceasefire and prompting U.S. missile strikes on southern Iraq.
Washington has pulled back military, aid and intelligence operations from Iraq, fearing Barzani's new ties to the central government in Baghdad would put U.S. personnel and their local staff at risk.
Baghdad's involvement in the Kurdish infighting has raised questions on the future of a U.S.-led no-fly zone over northern Iraq, set up in 1991 to protect the Kurds from any Iraqi attack.

The Kurdish leader crossed into Turkey in a black Mercedes on Wednesday morning, along with half a dozen vehicles carrying guards and aides. A Turkish military helicopter shadowed the convoy to Diyarbakir, where Barzani was flown to Ankara.
